pointers.sentence: `BaseDetailView.get` finds the object and keeps it as `BaseDetailView.object`, builds the context, and makes the response (`django/views/generic/detail.py:BaseDetailView.get`).
With neither it raises `AttributeError`, whose message says the view must be called with one or the other in the URLconf (`django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectMixin.get_object`).
The `LIMIT 21` in the query is that method's own doing, not the view's (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.get`).
In both cases what it returns is the result of `all()`, a new queryset (`django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectMixin.get_queryset`).

`get_queryset` gives each request a copy of it, made by `all()`, but code that evaluates the attribute itself, by iterating it or taking its length, fills the shared object's cache of rows, and every later request that evaluates it gets those rows in place of a query (`docs/ref/class-based-views/mixins-single-object.txt`, `django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._fetch_all`).

So the Gazette's template can say `"article"` where a template written for any model would say `"object"` (`django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectMixin.get_context_data`).

If nothing could be built it raises `ImproperlyConfigured` again, with a message that lists what would have helped (`django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectTemplateResponseMixin.get_template_names`).
`BaseListView.get` keeps the queryset as `BaseListView.object_list`, makes the context and makes the response (`django/views/generic/list.py:BaseListView.get`).

For the second page, `GET /articles/?page=2`, the rows are counted under `Paginator.page`, while the context is being made, since a page number cannot be validated without knowing how many rows there are (`django/core/paginator.py:Paginator.page`, `django/core/paginator.py:Paginator.count`).

And an ordering is applied at the end when there is one: `get_ordering` returns the `ordering` attribute, which is `None` unless it has been set to a field name or a sequence of them, and when it is set the queryset is passed through `order_by` (`django/views/generic/list.py:MultipleObjectMixin.get_queryset`).

Otherwise `paginate_queryset` takes over, and the context holds the paginator, the page as `"page_obj"`, the page's own objects as `"object_list"`, and `"is_paginated"`, which is true when there is more than one page (`django/views/generic/list.py:MultipleObjectMixin.get_context_data`).
A value that `int` refuses, other than the word `"last"`, is an `Http404`, and so is a number the paginator refuses (`django/views/generic/list.py:MultipleObjectMixin.paginate_queryset`).

With `allow_empty` false, `BaseListView.get` raises `Http404` for one, and takes care how it finds out: when `get_paginate_by` gives anything but `None` and the list is a queryset, it asks `exists`, a cheap query, where otherwise it tests the list for truth, which loads a queryset whole (`django/views/generic/list.py:BaseListView.get`).

Unlike the detail view's, this one adds the generated name even when `template_name` was given, so the given name is tried first and the generated one stands behind it (`django/views/generic/list.py:MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin.get_template_names`).
